item.title: Parliamentary Audit Committee Mandates Open Machine-Readable Procurement Ledgers
item.description:
GENEVA — A cross-party parliamentary audit panel passed sweeping transparency revisions Thursday requiring central ministries and state enterprises to publish contract price amendments in plain machine-readable ledgers within forty-eight hours of signature.

Historically, procurement portals posted initial winning bids while burying post-award change orders—where project budgets frequently doubled—inside scanned PDF annexes that civic watchdogs struggled to parse.

Tracking Beneficial Ownership Through Subcontractors

Under the updated statute, prime contractors exceeding $500,000 must disclose tiered subcontractor registries before treasury disbursements clear. Municipal comptrollers gain matching API access to flag split-tender evasion across regional hospital and road districts.
